proof:
Set $k=d-1$, $p=(d+1)/k$ and $B_d=(d+1)/(d-1)$. For $z>0$ and $|r|<z$,
$$
\left[\frac{(z+r)^p+(z-r)^p}{2}\right]^k
\ge z^{d+1}\bigl(1+B_d(r/z)^2\bigr).
$$
When $d=2$ this is the cubic identity with $k=1$. For $d\ge3$ one has $1<p\le2$, and the second derivative in $u=r/z$ of the normalized inner mean is at least $p(p-1)$ because the even mean of $(1\pm u)^{p-2}$ is at least one by convexity. Integrate twice from zero and use Bernoulli's inequality on the power $k$, with $kp(p-1)/2=B_d$.

Apply this bound to the scalar midpoint inequality in the optimized transport. If both arguments $s_1,s_2$ are at least $\delta$, put $l=(R(s_1)+R(s_2))/2=(s_1+s_2)/2$ and $\Delta=(R(s_1)-R(s_2))/2$. Dividing by $l^d$ bounds that inequality's left side below by $l+B_d\Delta^2/l$, hence by $l+c_d\Delta^2/l$. For the mixed branch put $s_1=\delta-2b$, $s_2=\delta+2r$ with $r\ge b\ge0$, and $z=\delta+r$. The true mean is $z-b$, while $l=z+db$ and $\Delta=db-r$. Apply the power inequality to $\delta,s_2$, and then divide by $(z-b)^d$. The quadratic Taylor bound $(1-u)^{-d}\ge1+du+d(d+1)u^2/2$ for $0\le u<1$ gives the lower bound
$$
z+db+\frac{B_dr^2+d(d+1)b^2/2}{z}.
$$
Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives $(r-db)^2\le [B_dr^2+d(d+1)b^2/2]/c_d$ because $1/B_d+2d/(d+1)=1/c_d$. Since $l\ge z$, the lower bound is at least $l+c_d\Delta^2/l$. If both arguments are at most $\delta$, the floor on the mean forces both to equal $\delta$, where $\Delta=0$.

The diagonal determinant bound of the optimized transport and substitution therefore give $\mu_K\ge(1+c_d\kappa^2)\zeta$, since $\kappa=|\Delta|/l$. Cauchy–Schwarz on a Borel $E$ gives the claimed restricted estimate. Apply it on the set selected by the midpoint cap bit in the common cap identity, for which the denominator defect is $\int_E\kappa\,d\zeta$, and also use $C_H\ge0$. For the total bound, the signed ratio $\Delta/l$ has $\zeta$-integral $(A-B)/2$ by the endpoint marginal identities, and $\zeta(F_K)=C/2$. Cauchy–Schwarz yields $c_d\int(\Delta/l)^2d\zeta\ge c_d(A-B)^2/(2C)$. The final expression follows by expanding $(A-B)^2=C^2-4AB$.

statement:
Use the optimized projective facet transport and its common cap identity. Write $\mu_K=f(L_K)\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{F_K}$, $c_d=(d+1)/(3d-1)$ and define $\kappa=|R_A-R_B|/(R_A+R_B)$ on the injectively parametrized midpoint image, with zero elsewhere. With $A,B$ the two optimized endpoint costs, $C=A+B$ and $M=\mu_K(F_K)$, one has
$$
\mu_K-\zeta\ge c_d\kappa^2\zeta,\qquad
\int_E\kappa\,d\zeta\le\sqrt{\zeta(E)(\mu_K-\zeta)(E)/c_d}
$$
for every Borel $E\subseteq F_K$. The same coupling for a closed cap or inward trace gives
$$
C_H\ge \max\{0,\zeta(H)-\sqrt{\zeta(H)(\mu_K-\zeta)(H)/c_d}\},
\qquad
M\ge C/2+\frac{c_d(A-B)^2}{2C}.
$$
Equivalently the last right side is $(1+c_d)C/2-c_d\,2AB/(A+B)$.
title: Quadratic control of the optimized facet transport defect
